subject: Mid-cycle collection notice — token rollback & payment authorization
messages:
From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@novametrics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kavita Rao <kavita@novametrics.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: mid-cycle collection notice — unexpected charge

Marcus,

We just received a collection notice this morning for an unexpected mid-cycle charge on our October invoice (INV-20261001). Our engineering team traced it to a sudden spike in embed counts around 2026-10-01T02:00Z after we flipped the streaming flag on a test service. We believe a small regression in our client produced duplicated partial requests that double-counted tokens for ~20 minutes.

Attached is a short sample export (novametrics-usage-sample-20261001.csv) showing the spike and the invoice PDF. Can Redwood pause collection while we reconcile? We need the charge explained or a rollback/credit applied — we cannot reconcile this on our ledger until the tokens are validated.

Appreciate a quick reply — this is blocking our internal finance hold.

Thanks,
Liam Chen
CTO, Novametrics
liam.chen@novametrics.com

--
Novametrics (external)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@novametrics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 10:08:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: mid-cycle collection notice — unexpected charge

Liam — thanks for flagging and for the sample. I’ve looped in Ben from Billing and Kimberly (your AM) so we can coordinate. We will not initiate a collection action while we investigate — I’ve asked Finance to hold the collection for 72 hours as a provisional measure.

Ben: can you pull token-level telemetry for Novametrics from 2026-10-01T01:50Z through 2026-10-01T03:00Z and share the session IDs? If there’s evidence of duplicate request IDs or partial-retry pathological behavior we will evaluate a rollback/credit. Please also pull any per-prefix caching/kv hits that could influence the counts.

Liam — two asks for now: 1) confirm whether you rolled a client change or enabled streaming at ~02:00Z, and 2) if you can attach the raw request ids (sample) that would speed the tie-out.

I’ll follow up once Ben has logs. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll move fast.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Lead — Billing Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Liam Chen <liam.chen@novametrics.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 08:56:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: mid-cycle collection notice — unexpected charge

Marcus/Kim/Liam — I pulled the initial telemetry and attached a short extract to this thread (see novametrics-usage-sample-20261001.csv referenced). Key findings so far:

- Between 2026-10-01T02:00:05Z and 2026-10-01T02:21:18Z we observed ~28k additional embed token attributions versus the 30-day baseline for the same time-of-day.
- There are ~420 request IDs where the client-supplied request_id header appears twice within a 30s window for the same session_id (possible retry/duplication).
- KV/prefix cache hit rates dropped ~62% during the window (suggesting cache-warm behavior after the streaming flip).

This looks consistent with a small client-side retry loop plus the client switching to streaming which caused partial frames to be ingested as separate usage events in our current counting pipeline. That would explain the double-count for short-lived sessions.

Next steps I propose: 1) we can produce a provisional credit equal to the excess tokens for that window pending final request-id tie-out, 2) Finance needs a signed authorization to waive collection or apply the credit to the invoice, 3) we’ll provide an exported evidence bundle (request_id list + timestamps) for Novametrics to reconcile.

Kimberly: can you send the standard credit-authorization form (for our accounting team) to Liam? Liam: if you can return the signed form we can apply the provisional credit and update the invoice.

Ben Carter
Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: novametrics-usage-sample-20261001.csv
From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@novametrics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Kavita Rao <kavita@novametrics.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: mid-cycle collection notice — unexpected charge

Thanks — Ben/Marcus. We confirmed the rollout: our infra team enabled streaming at 01:59Z and did not expect the client to surface partial frames as separate requests. We’ve pulled our request_id log and attached a sample set and the signed PO/authorization.

We appreciate the provisional credit offer. Kavita (finance) will sign the authorization and return it within the hour. Once the credit is applied can you confirm the adjusted invoice and whether any remaining balance will be re-scheduled? Also — please include the evidence bundle (request_id + timestamps) in the reply so our ledger team can perform the tie-out.

Liam Chen
CTO, Novametrics

Attachments: INV-20261001.pdf; novametrics-requestid-sample-20261001.csv; novametrics-credit-auth-signed.pdf
